title: The Khalsa Marks the Sahibzadas' Martyrdom Site

blocks.text: This transition page carries the narrative from the destruction of Sirhind into a work of remembrance. After identifying the places tied to the younger Sahibzadas, the Khalsa agrees that a single memorial shrine should be established so the memory of their martyrdom will remain embodied in a public sacred site.

Local elders are called to indicate the exact place and to recount what happened there in earlier days. The page therefore replaces the heat of battle with communal recollection, testimony, and the desire to anchor grief in durable form.

It also opens the next episode by showing that post-victory authority includes the power to consecrate memory. The Khalsa does not only punish Sirhind; it begins shaping how that punishment and martyrdom will be remembered.
